description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against occurrence result sets staged on a DataCanvas by paleobiology_search_occurrences. This is how you analyze a large fossil set without re-fetching it: count occurrences by early_interval, group by formation, country (cc), or accepted_name, or filter by a paleo/modern coordinate range. The classification column is JSON — roll up by rank with json_extract_string(classification, '$.family') (also $.phylum, $.class, $.order, $.genus). Staged rows are occurrences, so collection-only fields such as lithology are not present. Reference tables by the table_name that paleobiology_search_occurrences returned — call paleobiology_dataframe_describe first if you do not know the table or column names. A result too large to return inline comes back as its first rows, with a notice naming the ORDER BY … LIMIT/OFFSET that reads the rest. SELECT only; writes and file-reading functions are rejected.

canvas_id.description: Canvas id returned by paleobiology_search_occurrences when its result spilled.

sql.description: A read-only SQL SELECT. Reference tables by the names paleobiology_search_occurrences / paleobiology_dataframe_describe returned.

name: paleobiology_dataframe_query

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_disabled`: DataCanvas is not enabled on this deployment (CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE is not duckdb). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance when the result was cut to fit the inline response size (rows shown, the LIMIT/OFFSET that continues, and when to stop), when a single row was too large to show, or when row_count stopped at the canvas row cap.

row_count.description: Rows the query produced, counted up to the canvas row cap — exact unless truncated is true, when it equals the cap and the result is larger.

rows.description: Result rows in query order, ending at a whole row where more would exceed the inline response size. Keys are the selected column names. When rows were left out, the notice says how many are shown and the LIMIT/OFFSET that reads the rest.

truncated.description: True when the query produced more rows than the canvas row cap, so row_count stopped counting at the cap.

title: paleobiology-mcp-server: query staged occurrences with SQL
